append.text: **Ps 44:5a absolute *inténde, próspere procéde, et regna* → *atende, avança próspero, e reina*** — D3 kept where the Latin has no object (L&S: bow, course, mind; ἔντεινον 'bend'); the blind reader heard 'pay attention', odd before *avança* — the cost, flagged for Gustavo. *estende o arco* and *põe-te a caminho* are options (decision `intende`).
Ps 44:10b *Ástitit regína a dextris tuis* → *A rainha pôs-se à tua direita* — the split applied; the blind reader heard 'stood at your right'.
Ps 44:7 *virga directiónis virga regni tui* → *a vara do teu reino é vara de retidão* (natural order); the blind reader heard sceptre, 'stick' second.
Ps 44:13 *vultum tuum deprecabúntur* → *suplicarão o teu rosto* — the place this row named; heard as 'will entreat you'.
**Ps 44:2a *Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum* → *O meu coração fez jorrar uma boa palavra*** — held in its third place; no reader remarked on the verb.
Ps 44:7 *Sedes tua, Deus* → *O teu trono, ó Deus* (the king addressed as God).
Ps 44:15b *próximæ ejus* (αἱ πλησίον, the bride's companions) → *as que lhe são próximas* (the root kept; MS1932 *companheiras* would merge with 44:8 *consórtes*).

**Ps 44:12 *Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum* → *E o Rei ansiará pelo teu esplendor*** — held against the Latinist twice (minor: 'comeliness', *formosura*): *formosura* is *spécies*' two verses before (44:5a), *beleza* *pulchritúdo*'s, so the psalm's three words of beauty stay three.
Ps 44:12 *concupíscet Rex* → *o Rei ansiará por*; the stylist asked *desejará*, refused (118:20 has *concupíscere* and *desideráre* together).
**Ps 44 applies it:** 44:3 *Speciósus forma* → *mais formoso de aspecto*, 44:5a *Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua* → *Com a tua formosura e a tua beleza* (decor 44:12 *esplendor*).
Ps 44:13 *filhas de Tiro com dádivas* — held (the mediant proparoxytone, as *munéribus*); the stylist asked *ofertas*, refused (D41's *oferta*).

Not once: Ps 44:15b *Adducéntur Regi vírgines* → *Serão levadas ao Rei as virgens*, 44:16 *adducéntur in templum Regis* → *serão levadas ao templo do Rei* (grep), kept apart from *afférre* → trazer in the same verses.

**Ps 44:18a *in omni generatióne et generatiónem* → *de geração em geração*** — *omni* absorbed (MS1932 the same); the Latinist asked twice (minor) for *em toda geração e geração*, refused as not Portuguese, option. 144:13a has the same Latin and should copy it.
Ps 44:11 applied: *Ouve, filha, e vê, e inclina o teu ouvido* — the stylist's best line.
Ps 44:5b *dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua* → *a tua direita te guiará maravilhosamente*; heard as the right hand.

terms: | address — the psalmist to the Messiah-king (Ps 44) | *tu* (*O teu trono, ó Deus*), the bride *tu* too | open | Ps 44; D17 left it to this psalm. Rule 3 (a single human addressee); one song speaks to groom and bride with one address, as MS1932. Cost: 44:7–8 *ó Deus* in the *tu* form — the blind reader heard 44:7 as a turn to God. The whole *vós* text is option 2 (decision `address`; *Cingi-vos* at 44:4 because bare *Cingi* is also 'I girded'). Wants a ruling: 71 and 109:1–4 are near cousins |

| diffúndere | derramar (*derramou-se a graça nos teus lábios*) | open | Ps 44:3, the only place (grep); ἐξεχύθη, *effúndere*'s Greek, so D15 lets them share *derramar*. Verb-first kept so that the antiphon *Diffúsa est grátia* is sayable alone; the stylist's *nos teus lábios se derramou a graça* is the option |

| femur | coxa (*Cinge a tua espada sobre a tua coxa*) | open | Ps 44:4 (μηρός); the concrete image kept; MS1932 *ao teu lado* explains it; *cintura* option. v2: *Cinge a tua espada* (the stylist: *cingir* takes the sword as object) |

| gutta (the spice) | gota (*Mirra, e gota, e cássia*) | open | Ps 44:9; στακτή (DRB *stacte*). The Latin names the drop; the stylist asked *resina*, the blind reader found *gota* puzzling (drop or gout) — held, *resina* / *estacte* options |

| vestítus / vestiménta | veste / vestes | open | Ps 44:9 *a vestiméntis tuis* → *das tuas vestes*; 44:10b *in vestítu deauráto* → *em veste dourada* (the stylist: *vestido* is a modern dress). *vestítus* is ἱματισμός, as *vestis* at 21:19 (*veste*), so D15 lets them share. 101:27 *sicut opertórium … sicut vestiméntum* will need checking |

| várietas (of cloth) | cores variadas (*cercada de cores variadas*) | open | Ps 44:10b, 44:14 (*varietátibus*) — πεποικιλμένη; *variedade* failed the stylist and the blind reader ('assortment', vague); the plural *cores* also answers the number of 44:14. The gate Latinist (minor) wanted *variedade(s)* back: held, option |

| ab intus | de dentro (*Toda a glória da filha do Rei é de dentro*) | open | Ps 44:14 (ἔσωθεν); keeps *ab*, supplies only the copula; heard as inward, spiritual glory. *está no interior* (MS1932), *vem de dentro* (stylist) options |
| consórtes | companheiros (*acima dos teus companheiros*) | open | Ps 44:8 (μέτοχοι); *consortes* is a spouse in Portuguese. *præ* → *acima de* there (v2, stylist), *mais … que* at 44:3 |

| próspere (procédere) | próspero (*avança próspero*) | open | Ps 44:5a; the adjective for the adverb (the stylist; *com prosperidade* 'a finance report'); the gate Latinist preferred *prosperamente* (minor), option. 117:25 *prosperáre* → prosperar |
